## What changed or decided
Two files, both in task scope:

- **`tests/test_cca_completeness.py`** — replaced `MEASURED_SHORT_CIRCUIT_REASONS` with the **twelve verbatim** measured inputs (character-exact, no paraphrase). Diagnosis under the marker-only detector: ten were already rejected; **two survived** — `Deferred pending resolution of CCA-08` and `Blocked by CCA-08, so this was left unjudged`. Both name *another* item's id as the cause with **no failure word**, exactly the cross-item short-circuit the handoff describes. Added two guard genuine reasons: `CCA-06 has no durable artifact.` (external id ref, no skip cue → stays accepted, pins the two-signal rule) and a self-referencing `CCA-05 …` reason (own id + skip cue → stays accepted, pins self-reference exclusion).
- **`scripts/enforce_cca_verdict.py`** — replaced the failure-word-only `CCA_REFERENCE_FAILURE_RE` with `CCA_REFERENCE_RE` + `_references_external_item(...)`. A `CCA-<n>` reference whose id differs from the item being judged now counts as an external already-blocked cause; a reference to the item's **own** id is self-reference and does not count. Threaded the judged item's id (`item.get("id")` / `item.get("criterion")`) into the reason test at both call sites. The two-signal requirement is unchanged — a cause signal still needs a skip cue to trigger.
